content:
Yesterday's announcement of the Mac Studio with the M5 Max chip came with a bit of good news: the starting price remains the same as the previous-generation M4 Max Mac Studio, holding steady at $2,499.

However, if you want to upgrade the GPU, there's a hidden catch in the upgrade cost — it's actually $300 more than the price initially shown on Apple's website……

This hidden upgrade cost even caught John Gruber off guard while he was compiling the prices for various configurations of yesterday's new machines.

The base configuration of this machine comes with an 18-core CPU and a 32-core GPU. Apple's website lists the option to upgrade to a 40-core GPU, clearly marking an additional $300.

The catch is this: when you select this option, the memory also increases simultaneously from 32GB to 48GB, requiring an extra $300. Since it's not possible to upgrade only the GPU cores while keeping the original 32GB of memory, the actual upgrade cost is double the listed price, i.e., $600.

When you choose the upgraded chip, Apple reminds you of this in a slightly vague manner.

Are you tempted to upgrade to the new Mac Mini or Mac Studio models? Let us know in the comments section.
